claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: Daniel's exclamation of 'the world was ending' and 'nothing mattered anymore' constitutes an out-of-court statement.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) defines hearsay as an out-of-court statement.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact he exlaimed "the world was ending" and "nothing mattered anymore."

arguments.text: The exclamation contains explicit assertions regarding the state of the world and personal significance, rather than mere non-assertive conduct.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the out-of-court statement to be an assertion.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact he exlaimed "the world was ending" and "nothing mattered anymore."

arguments.text: The statement is offered to prove Daniel's emotional state (sadness) upon hearing the news, not to prove the truth of the asserted facts.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) excludes statements not offered for the truth of the matter asserted from the definition of hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: To prove that Daniel was sad upon hearing the news

arguments.text: Offering a statement to demonstrate the declarant's state of mind constitutes a recognized non-hearsay purpose, rendering the statement inadmissible as hearsay.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) and FRE 803(3) distinguish between hearsay and state-of-mind evidence; statements offered to show the declarant's condition are not hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: To prove that Daniel was sad upon hearing the news
